::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon="false" title="Purpose"}
Use this guide while completing the Week 1 readings and participating in class.
Your notes should help you recognize common data-structure mistakes before you
begin calculating statistics.
:::

## Objectives

- identify the unit of analysis and grain;
- distinguish observations, variables, values, and identifiers;
- evaluate whether a table follows tidy-data principles;
- distinguish dimensions from measures; and
- classify variables using appropriate measurement scales.

## 5) Distinguish dimensions and measures

- **Dimensions:** categories or identifiers used to group, filter, or label
  observations.
- **Measures:** numeric values that can be meaningfully summarized.

Record at least 2 examples of each from a course dataset.

## 7) Identify common analysis mistakes

For each mistake, explain how you would detect or prevent it:

- wrong unit of analysis;
- wrong data structure;
- wrong variable type;
- incorrect aggregation; and
- assuming a field means something without checking its documentation.
